title: How seeds travel
examples: Teacher, how do seeds get from one plant to another?
Can seeds really travel all by themselves?
What helps seeds move when the plant is not big?

explain.say: Seeds can travel in many different ways to new homes.
Wind can blow very light seeds over long distances.
Water can wash seeds away when it rains or floods.
Animals eat seeds and then move them when they poop.
Some pods pop open to shake seeds out everywhere.
When you throw a ball, you are using force to move it.

faq.q: Do all seeds travel the same way?
faq.a: No, seeds use different methods to travel to new places. Some float, some are carried by creatures.
asks: Is there one way seeds always travel?

faq.q: Are big seeds harder to move?
faq.a: Yes, bigger seeds usually need more help to move far. They might need an animal or a big current of water.
asks: Do big seeds need help to travel?

faq.q: Do animals always help seeds travel?
faq.a: Not always, but many animals eat seeds and help spread them. Sometimes they just carry them on their fur.
asks: What if animals just carry seeds?

faq.q: What is the difference between wind and water travel?
faq.a: Wind moves things through the air, like dandelion fluff. Water moves things through liquids, like a stream.
asks: Is wind like water for seeds?
Which is stronger, wind or water?

faq.q: What happens after the seeds land somewhere new?
faq.a: If the new spot has good soil and enough sun, the seed can start to grow into a new plant.
asks: What does a seed need to start growing?

facts: Some seeds have fluffy parts to catch the wind.
Seeds can travel inside the fruit that an animal eats.
Water can carry seeds down rivers to new banks.
Some plants make pods that shake to release seeds.

quiz.say: Dandelion seeds are best at traveling by:
quiz.why: Dandelion seeds are very light and fluffy, which helps the wind blow them far away.

wrong.1: Water usually needs the seeds to be heavy or stuck to something floating.
wrong.2: While animals can carry things, dandelion seeds are designed to float on the air.
wrong.3: Popping pods help them start moving, but the wind is what carries them the farthest.

quiz.say: If a seed is carried by a river, what force is moving it?
quiz.why: Rivers are made of water, so the water current pushes the seeds along.

wrong.0: The river itself is the force, not necessarily an animal pushing it.
wrong.1: Gravity pulls things down, but the river current pushes them along.
wrong.3: Air moves things like leaves or fluff, but a river is liquid.

quiz.say: Which method relies on the seed being eaten first?
quiz.why: When an animal eats a seed inside a fruit, the seed passes out later.

wrong.1: Wind moves seeds that are already outside the plant.
wrong.2: Water moves seeds that are floating or washed away.
wrong.3: Popping pods release seeds directly, without an animal eating them first.
